notes: Account: product-led mid-market SaaS providing enterprise search for vertical B2B apps.
Primary goal: replace brittle TF-IDF search + ad-hoc embeddings with robust semantic layer + vector DB integration.
Initial evaluation started with Hosted API (Jan POC). Team liked API ergonomics and streaming but flagged cost/throughput concerns for nightly bulk ingestion.

POC summary: built prototype pipeline using Hosted embeddings -> Pinecone. Ingested 60k docs (120k vectors) over 48h. Query testing: 150 qps sustained with p95 lookup ~85ms (too high for product SLO).
Current ask: can Redwood meet nightly batch ingestion 200k vectors/day, and p95 lookup <40ms at 300-400 qps? Also want predictable unit economics for capacity planning.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, customer-managed KMS, audit logs; data residency requirement for EU customers (some workloads will be EU-only).
Quote from CTO (Anika Rao): 'We need predictable performance — can't have search slowdowns during demo accounts or spikes from scheduled batch jobs.'
Pricing sensitivity: tight margins; target TCO reduction vs current pinecone + self-hosted encoders of ~25% year-1.
Noted integration: team uses PostgreSQL + Airflow for ETL, and wants easy fall-through to Milvus in future. Interested in Redwood's batching/caching suggestions.
Internal stakeholders: Product (Samir - PM), Infra (Anika - CTO), Data Eng (Ravi), Security (Erin).
Redwood strengths flagged by team: transparent perf profiles, routing/fallback options, rollout controls. Concerns: Dedicated pricing and migration path from Hosted during trial.
We provided Hosted POC perf logs, suggested Dedicated sizing template; SE (Maya) ran a config sim for 2 GPU pool variants.
Legal: standard DPA ok; data residency clause needs sign-off (legal team asked for Redwood private deployment options).
